verdict: Use only two main-deck bridge candidates; keep appendix and superseded assets out of the core result spine.
deck_rule: At most one human organoid bridge and at most one OSD-120/multispecies bridge; v1-v7 benchmark result slides remain the core.

candidates.title: Human organoid source-to-matrix
candidates.rationale: Shows official OSDR pages becoming downloaded expression matrices. Good first-view explanation for how organoid data enters v9.
candidates.guardrail: Draft pilot only; not mission-held-out and not a final benchmark result.

candidates.title: OSD-120 source-to-task
candidates.rationale: Explains how one OSDR study becomes a constrained task check with held-out groups and visible sample balance.
candidates.guardrail: Same-study only; not mission-held-out and not cross-species generalization.

candidates.title: OSDR source-record contact sheet
candidates.rationale: Efficient proof that OSD-863, OSD-871, OSD-120, and OSD-918 official source records were captured.
candidates.guardrail: Use as receipt material; do not turn it into a main-story methods slide.

candidates.title: Extension source lanes
candidates.rationale: Useful for showing organoid, plant, and single-cell lanes as possible extensions around the v9 provenance layer.
candidates.guardrail: Keep behind the core deck unless extension scope is explicitly discussed.

candidates.title: Earlier organoid source proof
candidates.rationale: The newer organoid panel explains the local matrix step more clearly and uses cleaner audience-facing text.
candidates.guardrail: Do not use in main deck unless the v0.2 panel fails slide-level QA.

candidates.title: Earlier OSD-120 source proof
candidates.rationale: The newer OSD-120 panel better explains the held-out task and avoids overly internal wording.
candidates.guardrail: Keep only as provenance backup, not as a slide candidate.
